| Endpoint family | Returns | Shape |
|---|---|---|
| single article | `ArticleRO` | `{ article: {...} }` |
| list | `ArticlesRO` | `{ articles: [...], articlesCount: n }` |
| comments | `CommentsRO` | `{ comments: [...] }` |
| user | `UserRO` | `{ user: {..., token} }` |
| profile | `ProfileRO` | `{ profile: {..., following} }` |

The frontends read `response.article.slug`, `response.user.token`, etc. A method that returns a
bare entity instead of the envelope breaks every RealWorld client (see `LESSONS.md`).

### [LESSONS.md] LESSONS.md > Lessons Learned — RealWorld API (NestJS) > Authentication is not authorization (#6, #44)
**What happened:** any logged-in user could `PUT` or `DELETE` any other user's article. The
route is in `AuthMiddleware`'s list, so people assumed it was "protected" — but the middleware
only proves the caller is *a* user, and `ArticleService.update()/delete()` never compare
`req.user.id` with `article.author.id`. The Swagger `403 Forbidden` annotations on those handlers
describe a check that does not exist.

**Rule:** for every mutating route, name the line that compares the caller with the record's
owner. If you cannot, there is no ownership check, whatever the decorators say.

```
src/

  app.module.ts           imports Article/User/Profile/Tag modules
  config.ts               SECRET (not committed; copy config.ts.example)
  article/                articles + comments + favourites
    article.controller.ts / article.service.ts / article.entity.ts / comment.entity.ts
    article.interface.ts  ArticleRO, ArticlesRO, CommentsRO
    dto/                  CreateArticleDto, CreateCommentDto
  user/                   registration, login, current user, AuthMiddleware, @User() decorator
  profile/                profiles + follow/unfollow (FollowsEntity)
  tag/                    GET /tags only
  shared/pipes/           ValidationPipe
```

One module per RealWorld resource. Each module owns its controller, service, entity and DTOs.
Module files also own **which routes require auth** — see `auth.md`.

| `UserModule` | `GET /user`, `PUT /user` |

### [.claude/knowledge/auth.md] auth.md > Authentication and authorization > Authorization (ownership) — where it is enforced

compares the caller with the record's owner:

| Action | Ownership check |
|---|---|
| `PUT /articles/:slug` | none — `ArticleService.update(slug, body)` does `Object.assign(article, body)` and saves |
| `DELETE /articles/:slug` | none — `delete({slug})` |
| `DELETE /articles/:slug/comments/:id` | none — and comments have no author to compare against anyway |
| `DELETE /users/:slug` | none, and unguarded |
| `PUT /user` | implicitly the caller (`@User('id')`), fine |

The Swagger `@ApiResponse({ status: 403 })` lines on the article controller describe an
intended behaviour, not an implemented one — nothing returns 403.

### [.claude/knowledge/auth.md] auth.md > Authentication and authorization > Two ways a request learns who the user is > 2. `@User()` decorator — `src/user/user.decorator.ts` (optional identity, no guard)
Used as `@User('id')`, `@User('email')`, or bare `@User()` on handler parameters.
- If the middleware ran, returns `req.user[data]` (or the whole user).
- Otherwise it decodes the token itself with `jwt.verify` and returns `decoded[data]` — so a
  route that is NOT in the middleware list can still see who is calling **if** a token is
  sent, and gets `undefined` if none is. (Bare `@User()` on an unguarded route returns
  `decoded.user`, which does not exist in the payload → `undefined`.)
- Same `jwt.verify` throw → 500 problem as the middleware.

**What happened:** `ArticleController.create()` returned `ArticleEntity` directly while every

from its side the request succeeded.

**Rule:** the envelope (`ArticleRO`, `UserRO`, …) is the contract with every RealWorld client.
A handler whose return type is not a `*RO` interface is a bug even if it "works" in Postman.

with no eager flag. See `schema.md` for what that means for service code.

### [LESSONS.md] LESSONS.md > Lessons Learned — RealWorld API (NestJS) > Static routes are declared before parameterised ones (#7)
**What happened:** `GET /articles/feed` was declared *after* `GET /articles/:slug`, so Nest
matched `feed` as a slug and the feed endpoint returned `{ article: undefined }`. Fixed by moving
`getFeed()` above `findOne()` in `ArticleController`.

**Rule:** in a controller, any literal path (`feed`, `popular`, `search`) goes above the `:slug`
handler. Order in the class is match order.

### [.claude/knowledge/workspace.md] workspace.md > RealWorld API (NestJS) — workspace overview > Conventions (these are the rules, not suggestions) > Request bodies are nested too
Handlers read `@Body('article')`, `@Body('user')`, `@Body('comment')` — the client sends
`{ "article": {...} }`, never a flat object. New endpoints follow the same nesting.

### [.claude/knowledge/workspace.md] workspace.md > RealWorld API (NestJS) — workspace overview > Conventions (these are the rules, not suggestions) > DTOs
Plain classes in `dto/`, `readonly` fields. Only `CreateUserDto` carries `class-validator`
decorators (`@IsNotEmpty`); `UpdateUserDto`, `CreateArticleDto`, `CreateCommentDto` have none.
The custom `ValidationPipe` is applied **per handler** with `@UsePipes(new ValidationPipe())`
— it is not global. Today only `POST /users` and `POST /users/login` use it.

### [LESSONS.md] LESSONS.md > Lessons Learned — RealWorld API (NestJS) > A lifecycle hook that hashes on insert does not run on update (#88)
**What happened:** `PUT /user` with `{ "user": { "password": "newpassword" } }` wrote the string
`newpassword` into the `password` column. `UserEntity.hashPassword()` is `@BeforeInsert()` only;
`UserService.update()` does `Object.assign(toUpdate, dto)` and saves, so the plaintext went
straight to MySQL. Users who changed their password could never log in again — `argon2.verify`
compares the typed password against a non-hash and fails.

**Rule:** every write path a secret can travel must hash it explicitly, and `@BeforeInsert`
covers exactly one of them. When you see a hook, ask which lifecycle events it does NOT cover.

### [.claude/knowledge/auth.md] auth.md > Authentication and authorization > Two ways a request learns who the user is > 1. `AuthMiddleware` — `src/user/auth.middleware.ts` (the guard)
Applied **per route, per module**, in each module's `configure(consumer)`. Behaviour:
- no `Authorization` header, or nothing after the space → `HttpException('Not authorized.', 401)`
- header present → `jwt.verify(token, SECRET)` → `userService.findById(decoded.id)` → sets
  `req.user = user.user` and calls `next()`.
- `jwt.verify` **throws** on an expired, malformed or wrongly-signed token, and nothing in the
  middleware catches it — the framework turns that into a **500**, not a 401 (see `LESSONS.md`).
- `findById` throws `HttpException({errors}, 401)` if the id no longer exists.

### [.claude/knowledge/schema.md] schema.md > Data model (TypeORM entities, `synchronize: true`) > `comment` — `src/article/comment.entity.ts`
| column | type |
|---|---|
| id | int PK |
| body | varchar |
| articleId | FK → article |

**There is no author column and no relation to `user`.** The RealWorld spec's comment object
has `author`; this entity cannot produce it. `addComment()` sets only `body`.

### [LESSONS.md] LESSONS.md > Lessons Learned — RealWorld API (NestJS) > Never `Object.assign` a request body onto a persisted entity (#112)
**What happened:** `UserService.update()` and `ArticleService.update()` both merge the raw body
into the loaded entity. Any extra field the client sends — `id`, `password`, `authorId`,
`favoriteCount` — is persisted. The DTO type is a TypeScript annotation; it strips nothing at
runtime, and `PUT /user` / `PUT /articles/:slug` have no validation pipe.

**Rule:** copy the allowed fields by name, or whitelist with a validation pipe
(`whitelist: true, forbidNonWhitelisted: true`). The DTO class is not a filter.

text:
**Refined prompt:** Three separate questions about this NestJS RealWorld API, answered as a security reviewer who assumes a hostile caller and cites the enforcing line or states there is none: (1) does `deleteComment` verify the caller authored the comment — trace the authorization decision and say whether the exposure is reachable; (2) enumerate which `profiles/*` routes `AuthMiddleware` is applied to and which are therefore public; (3) explain what the `RO` suffix on the `*.interface.ts` types denotes.

---

## 1. `deleteComment` — no, there is no author check, and there cannot be one

**The exposure.** Any authenticated user can delete any comment on any article.

The full trace, caller → storage:

| Step | Line | What it does with caller identity |
|---|---|---|
| Route guard | `src/article/article.module.ts:29` | `DELETE articles/:slug/comments/:id` is in the `AuthMiddleware` list → proves a valid token, nothing more |
| Handler | `src/article/article.controller.ts:85-88` | `async deleteComment(@Param() params)` — **no `@User('id')` parameter**. The caller's identity never enters the handler |
| Service | `src/article/article.service.ts:114-129` | `deleteComment(slug, id)` — loads article by slug, loads comment by id, splices, deletes. No `userId` argument exists to compare |
| Entity | `src/article/comment.entity.ts:5-15` | columns `id`, `body`, `@ManyToOne` → `ArticleEntity`. **No `author` relation** |

**The enforcement point that should stop it** would be in `ArticleService.deleteComment()` — a comparison of `req.user.id` against `comment.author.id` before `commentRepository.delete()` at `article.service.ts:122`. That line does not exist, and it cannot be written today: `Comment` has no author column, so there is no owner to compare against. Fixing this requires a schema change first (add `@ManyToOne(() => UserEntity)` to `Comment`, set it in `addComment()` at `article.service.ts:101-112`, which currently sets only `body`), then the check. This matches the design note already open in `CURRENT_FOCUS.md`.

**Is it reachable?** Yes, today, with any valid token. The `@ApiResponse({ status: 403, description: 'Forbidden.' })` on `article.controller.ts:83` documents a check that was never implemented — nothing in this path returns 403.

Two things on the traced path that are *not* ownership checks but are easy to mistake for one:

- `article.service.ts:118-120` — the `deleteIndex >= 0` test only confirms the comment belongs to the **article in the URL**. It's a containment check, not authorization. It does mean you must name the correct `:slug` to delete a comment, which is no obstacle: `GET /api/articles/:slug/comments` is public.
- `article.service.ts:117-118` — `commentRepository.findOne(id)` returns `undefined` for a nonexistent id, and `comment.id` on the next line then throws a `TypeError` → 500 rather than 404.

## 2. Profile routes behind `AuthMiddleware`

`ProfileModule.configure()` applies it to exactly one path, all methods (`src/profile/profile.module.ts:19-23`):

```ts
.forRoutes({path: 'profiles/:username/follow', method: RequestMethod.ALL});
```

Resolved against the controller, with the `/api` global prefix from `main.ts:8`:

| Route | Handler | Guarded? |
|---|---|---|
| `POST /api/profiles/:username/follow` | `profile.controller.ts:23-26` | **Yes** — 401 without a token |
| `DELETE /api/profiles/:username/follow` | `profile.controller.ts:28-31` | **Yes** — 401 without a token |
| `GET /api/profiles/:username` | `profile.controller.ts:18-21` | **No** — public |

`RequestMethod.ALL` means the guard is on the path, not the verb, so any method later added at `:username/follow` is covered automatically — but nothing else under `profiles/` is.

On the unguarded `GET /api/profiles/:username`: its `@User('id')` parameter is not a guard. The decorator (`src/user/user.decorator.ts:5-18`) falls through to decoding the token itself when no middleware ran, returning `undefined` if no token is sent — that's intended optional identity, used to compute `following`. Note it calls `jwt.verify` at line 15 with no try/catch, so a malformed or expired token on this public route surfaces as a 500, not a 401 — same defect as the middleware at `auth.middleware.ts:17`.

## 3. `RO` = Response Object

It's the RealWorld JSON envelope — the single top-level key every client reads through. Each module declares its own in `*.interface.ts`:

| Type | Declared at | Shape |
|---|---|---|
| `UserRO` | `user/user.interface.ts:9-11` | `{ user: UserData }` |
| `ProfileRO` | `profile/profile.interface.ts:8-10` | `{ profile: ProfileData }` |
| `ArticleRO` | `article/article.interface.ts:24-26` | `{ article: ArticleEntity }` |
| `ArticlesRO` | `article/article.interface.ts:28-31` | `{ articles: ArticleEntity[], articlesCount: number }` |
| `CommentsRO` | `article/article.interface.ts:20-22` | `{ comments: Comment[] }` |

Frontends read `response.article.slug`, `response.user.token` — a handler returning a bare entity breaks every client. Request bodies mirror the same nesting (`@Body('article')`, `article.controller.ts:52`).

One thing worth flagging, since it's about what `RO` does and doesn't guarantee: the suffix constrains the *wrapper*, not the payload. `ArticleRO.article` is typed `ArticleEntity` (`article.interface.ts:25`), not the spec-shaped `ArticleData` declared just above it at lines 7-18 — that interface is currently unused. So the envelope passes the raw entity through. Combined with `leftJoinAndSelect('article.author', 'author')` at `article.service.ts:30` and `password` having no `select: false` on `user.entity.ts:25-26`, and no `ClassSerializerInterceptor` registered anywhere (`main.ts`, `app.module.ts`), **`GET /api/articles` returns every author's argon2 password hash** — unauthenticated. That's a separate finding from your three questions; say the word and I'll trace it properly rather than assert it off a read-through.

---

All three parts addressed: (1) no author verification in `deleteComment`, exposure reachable by any authenticated user, blocked from being fixed by the missing `Comment.author` relation; (2) only `POST` and `DELETE /profiles/:username/follow` are guarded, `GET /profiles/:username` is public; (3) `RO` = Response Object, the RealWorld envelope, typed per module in `*.interface.ts`.
